Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old woman with several days of progressive, constant lower midline abdominal pain, requesting evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Constant lower (suprapubic) abdominal pain for a few days, progressively worsening; pain rated ~8/10.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Nausea with urge to vomit but no vomiting.
  - Light vaginal bleeding/discharge described as light pink and different from usual menses.
  - Constipation last week (resolved this week).
  - Normal oral intake and usual activities preserved.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting.
  - No reported fever or feeling feverish.
  - No fainting or presyncope.
  - No reported dysuria, frequency, or strong-smelling urine.
  - No shoulder pain or breathing difficulty.
  - Bowel movements reported as normal this week.
- Menstrual/gynecologic:
  - Last period approximately 2–3 weeks ago; patient states period stopped ~2 weeks ago.
  - Uses Implanon implant for contraception placed ~1 year ago.
  - No prior pregnancies.
  - Pregnancy test performed about 1 month ago (result not documented).
- Past medical history / allergies / medications:
  - Allergy: amoxicillin (allergy documented).
  - No prior surgeries reported.
  - No regular medications reported aside from contraceptive implant (Implanon) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history / preventive care:
  - Occupation: school teacher.
  - Lives with husband and his family.
  - Smoking/drinking status unclear (patient replied "I don't know" when asked).
  - Recent travel: none recently; previous travel ~1 year ago (unclear details).

Examination:
- (No vital signs or physical examination findings documented; face-to-face exam planned.)

Impression:
- Acute, progressive lower midline abdominal pain of uncertain etiology; associated light vaginal bleeding/discharge and nausea. Cause not determined via remote consult.

Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face clinic appointment for abdominal and pelvic examination (patient to call support line to book).
- Patient to perform a pregnancy test today; if positive, patient advised to contact service immediately for urgent review.
- Advise earlier re-presentation if symptoms significantly worsen (e.g., unable to keep fluids down) or new concerning features develop.
- Further assessment and management to be determined after in-person examination.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Recent pregnancy test result (patient reported one ~1 month ago but result not documented); no pregnancy test result from today.
  - Vital signs and physical examination findings.
  - Medication reconciliation (exact current medications besides implant not fully documented).
  - Laboratory or imaging results (none performed/documented).
  - STI screen, urinalysis, or pregnancy test result pending.
- Internal conflicts / unclear statements:
  - Timing of recent sexual intercourse: patient stated both “four weeks ago” and “four days ago” (conflict/uncertain).
  - Smoking/drinking status: patient answered “I don't know” (unclear).
  - Patient response to question about weight loss or blood in stool/urine was unclear; she subsequently described vaginal discharge and pain (uncertain).
- Transcript quality:
  - Moderately poor in places with intermittent inaudible or unclear phrases; occasional patient difficulty hearing and brief conversational confusion.
